name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
description: A texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, generated using text-to-image models with texture-specific prompts and a three-stage refinement process consisting of frequency analysis, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring.
rai:dataCollection: Images were generated using Stable Diffusion text-to-image models based on constructed texture-specific prompts. The generation process involved creating 96,768 unique prompts by combining descriptors across categories (artistic, spatial, color enhancer, color, and texture), with 5 images generated per prompt, resulting in 483,840 initial images before refinement.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were generated synthetically using Stable Diffusion model pipelines from HuggingFace, with prompts constructed from combinations of texture descriptors. The texture classes were based on 47 classes from the Describable Textures Dataset (DTD) plus 9 additional texture classes, totaling 56 texture classes.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images flagged by the NSFW safety filter were regenerated to ensure a consistent number of images per prompt. Flagged images were excluded from the final dataset for ethical reasons, despite not containing actual explicit content.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied: (1) Frequency filtering using Fourier transforms to remove object-like images by retaining the top 80% of images with highest frequency cutoff values; (2) Patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images by filtering out the bottom 20% of images with lowest mean patch variance (50x50 pixel patches); (3) CLIP score filtering to ensure prompt alignment by filtering out the bottom 20% of images with lowest CLIP scores within each texture class. This reduced the dataset from 483,840 to 246,285 images.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation was conducted with 9 participants who evaluated 100 images each (900 unique images total). Participants rated images on two dimensions: (1) overall quality and (2) representativeness to the provided descriptor, using a scale of 1 to 5.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation scores were analyzed across different refinement stages to validate the effectiveness of each filtering step. CLIP scores were found to align well with human representative scores, confirming CLIP's effectiveness in measuring prompt-image alignment for texture data.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each evaluated image received 1 quality rating and 1 representativeness rating from a single human evaluator.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) was used for automated scoring to measure alignment between prompts and generated images. Stable Diffusion's built-in NSFW content safety filter was used during generation.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables research on texture bias in machine learning models, which has implications for understanding model interpretability, uncovering biases, and identifying security vulnerabilities. The work demonstrates that models exhibit texture bias and that texture data can be exploited to create adversarial examples.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset generation process encountered challenges with NSFW safety filters, with up to 60% of initial images being flagged despite using benign prompts. Certain texture descriptors like 'paisley' consistently triggered the filter. The analysis revealed that high NSFW flagging rates are a broader issue with generating texture images rather than being limited to specific prompts. Variation in quality was observed across texture classes, with textures appearing in common objects (e.g., hairy, flaky) performing better than more structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted).
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is synthetically generated and may not capture all nuances of real-world textures. Certain texture classes showed lower quality scores, particularly more structured textures like grid and polka-dotted patterns. The methodology relies on text-to-image models that were not explicitly designed for texture generation, which may introduce artifacts or non-texture elements. Some word pairings in prompts were found to be more compatible than others, affecting resulting image quality.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for texture-based research including: understanding high-level features models learn, uncovering biases in machine learning models, identifying security vulnerabilities, measuring texture bias through Texture Object Association Values (TAV), constructing texture-object associations, and creating adversarial examples. The dataset has been used to measure texture bias and identify that texture type can affect model accuracy by up to 66% and confidence by 40% on clean validation data.
